newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-CARLING UNEXPECTEDLY RETAINS PLACE AHEAD OF GUSCOTT.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-CARLING UNEXPECTEDLY RETAINS PLACE AHEAD OF GUSCOTT.

text.p: Former England rugby union captain Will Carling was unexpectedly selected on Wednesday for the international against Italy at Twickenham on November 23.
His exclusion had been widely predicted after Phil Glanville, also a a centre, was named on Tuesday as his successor as national skipper.

However, England have instead dropped Jeremy Guscutt, although he is a Bath club mate of de Glanville's. The pair have a good understanding in the centres nurtured under current England manager Jack Rowell when he coached Bath.
Carling, 30, who has won 66 England caps, a record 59 as captain, gave up the skipper's job but always hoped to remain in the team.
He was in fine early season form for his club Harlequins, although he has recently experimented at fly-half.
In all, England show seven changes, one positional, from the team who beat Ireland in March.
Newcastle full-back Tim Stimpson, Bath wing Adedayo Adebayo, Wasps scrum-half Andy Gomarsall and Bristol lock Simon Shaw are the new caps.
"Guscott was disappointed and surprised and expressed his disappointment to me," England manager Jack Rowell said.
"He has ambitions to return to England and to play for the Lions. But Will edged him out on this occasion in consultation with the new captain Phil.
"It was a difficult decision because both the traditional centres have been playing well.
"But we must not underestimate the number of times that de Glanville probably deserved to play, but was left out."

England - Tim Stimpson; Jon Sleightholme, Phil de Glanville (captain), Will Carling, Adebayo Adebayo; Mike Catt, Andy Gomarsall; Ben Clarke, Tim Rodber, Lawrence Dallaglio, Martin Johnson, Simon Shaw, Graham Rowntree, Mark Regan, Jason Leonard.
